 WTA Tokyo Round of 16 Best Bets Including Elena Rybakina vs Yulia Putintseva 
 Share Share this article
 × X Facebook LinkedIn WhatsApp Reddit Email Copy 
 The WTA Tokyo tournament, also known as the Pan Pacific Open, begins in Japan. This is a WTA 500 event, but it has no bearing on the upcoming WTA Finals and the race to Indian Wells. That competition is over, with the WTA formally announcing in early November that all eight singles players have qualified. The Pan Pacific Open therefore becomes a straightforward tournament where players are trying to build their rankings for the start of the 2027 season and earn prize money. A 500-point tournament offers the chance to make a major gain in the rankings. It’s a lot more than a WTA 250. Let’s see which players still have the energy and form to make a run at this late-season tournament and build confidence heading into the offseason. Fall tennis differs from spring or summer tennis because some players are more tired at this point in the year, opening the door for others to make their mark at this 2026 WTA Tokyo event. LWOS has our best bets for three matches. Post your best bets and thoughts in the comments. 
 WTA Tokyo 
 Fernandez – Mertens: 22:00 EST 
 H2H: 2-2 
 In this WTA Tokyo match, we have a rematch of a very recent meeting in Ningbo. Leylah Fernandez beat Elise Mertens 7-5 in the third set. Because these two just played a three-setter with Fernandez winning, it is logical to expect Mertens to gain revenge. It is logical to trust Fernandez’s recent momentum. It is logical to expect a close match. Which bet makes the most sense? 
 Best Bet to Make 
 This WTA Tokyo match could go either way, if we are being honest. The best play is over 2.5 sets, since the last meeting in Ningbo went three sets. These are evenly matched players. We’re not taking a Mertens victory because Fernandez is 4-1 in her last five matches. She is playing better than Mertens, so she will win at least one set. Mertens, motivated by revenge, also wins at least one set, but we don’t have to pick a match winner. Over 2.5 sets feels like the better play for more value. 
 That being said, betting on over 2.5 sets is a value bet for sure. 
 Value bet/ the best odds: over 2.5 sets @2.38 @betsson 
 Osaka – Pohankova: 00:30 EST 
 H2H: 0-0 
 This WTA Tokyo match looks very straightforward. Naomi Osaka beat Jasmine Paolini in straight sets. Paolini is a top-35 player. Mia Pohankova, Osaka’s next opponent, is ranked over 100 spots lower than Paolini. Osaka is playing at home in Japan. Just how close can Pohankova make this match?  
 Jun 2, 2023; Paris,France; Elise Mertens (BEL) celebrates winning her match against Jessica Pegula (USA) on day six at Stade Roland-Garros. Mandatory Credit: Susan Mullane-USA TODAY Sports | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Yesh Ginsburg 
 Best Bet to Make 
 This WTA Tokyo match will end only one way, with Osaka winning in straight sets. A lot of matches are hard to predict. This is one of the rare ones that looks pretty obvious. Osaka beat a good player, Paolini, in straight sets. It’s hard to think Pohankova will do better than Paolini. 
 That being said, betting on Osaka winning 2:0 is a value bet for sure. 
 Value bet/ the best odds: Osaka winning 2:0 @1.72 @1xBet 
 Rybakina – Putintseva: 3:00 EST 
 H2H: 2-2 
 This WTA Tokyo match features two players who are playing really well right now. Elena Rybakina and Yulia Putintseva are both 5-1 in their last six matches. Rybakina is the World No. 1 player on the WTA Tour, so she will naturally be heavily favored to win. Rybakina to win in straight sets is priced at 1.48, which is not a high-value bet, so this is a game spread bet. 
 Best Bet to Make 
 This WTA Tokyo match is a game spread bet. Because Putintseva is playing well and yet is priced as a huge underdog, betting on Putintseva against the game spread makes sense. We suggest keeping this one simple. No need to overthink a match like this one.  
 That being said, betting on Putintseva +6.5 games is a value bet for sure. 
 Value bet/ the best odds: Putintseva +6.5 games @1.60 @Interwetten
